english: Let $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $f(x)=x+\log_{e}\left(x^{2}-2x+2\right)$. Then which of the following is TRUE?
hindi: माना कि $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=x+\log_{e}\left(x^{2}-2x+2\right)$ द्वारा परिभाषित है। तब निम्न में से कौन-सा सत्य है?
solution: $x^{2}-2x+2=(x-1)^{2}+1>0$; $f'(x)=1+\dfrac{2x-2}{x^{2}-2x+2}=\dfrac{x^{2}}{x^{2}-2x+2}\ge 0$, zero only at $x=0$, so $f$ is strictly increasing on $\mathbb{R}$; $f(0)=\log_e 2$.
solution_full: Domain: $x^{2}-2x+2=(x-1)^{2}+1\ge 1>0$ for all real $x$, so $f$ is defined and differentiable on $\mathbb{R}$.
So $f'(x)\ge 0$ for all $x$, with equality only at the single point $x=0$. Hence $f$ is strictly increasing on $\mathbb{R}$ (always increasing), and $a<b\Rightarrow f(a)<f(b)$. Also $f(0)=\log_{e}2$.

(A) $f\left(\frac13\right)=\frac13+\log_{e}\frac{13}{9}$. Since $\frac13>0$, $f\left(\frac13\right)>\log_{e}2$, i.e. $\frac13>\log_{e}\frac{18}{13}$, so $e^{1/3}>\frac{18}{13}$ and $e>\left(\frac{18}{13}\right)^{3}$. Statement (A) says the opposite, so (A) is wrong.
(D) $f\left(-\frac12\right)=-\frac12+\log_{e}\frac{13}{4}<\log_{e}2$, so $\log_{e}\frac{13}{8}<\frac12$, i.e. $\sqrt{e}>\frac{13}{8}$ and $e>\frac{169}{64}$. So (D) is correct.
Each wrong option is exactly the reversed inequality obtained by treating $f$ as decreasing.
originality_note: New: one always-increasing function f(x)=x+ln(x^2-2x+2) generates four close numerical bounds on e at x = 1/3, -1/3, 1/2, -1/2 (way 5). Closest known: proving e^x > 1+x or x > ln(1+x) by monotonicity. Different because: the comparison numbers (18/13)^3, (25/18)^3, 169/64 are within 2% of e and come only from evaluating f at chosen points.

concept_use.Always increasing/always decreasing base: f'(x) = x^2/(x^2-2x+2) >= 0 with a single zero, so f is increasing on the whole real line.
concept_use.Proving inequalities using monotonicity: Each option is f(a) compared with f(0) for a = 1/3, -1/3, 1/2, -1/2, converted into a bound on e.

stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol, curve and function introduced with its domain; conditions complete; one reading of each sentence; answer unique and equal to the plan (Option D); Hindi mirrors the English maths. Checked exactly one statement (D) is true and all four come from f at a point. No change.
key_step: Simplify f' to x^2/(x^2-2x+2) and compare f at the four points with f(0).
justification: A routine chain (derivative simplification, monotonicity, four substitutions) with no insight, as in the monotonicity anchors 2024-P2-Q10 (L1) and 2021-P1-Q12 (L2); four evaluations push it to 2.
